about: What fire does to the voxels of an object (web/systems/burn.js, web/systems/fireSim.js). Each part of an object (its role: trunk, canopy, stone, water) has a material; a stone part whose palette is named in `palettes` has that material instead (the wooden crates and beams are stone parts with the wood palette). A material: burns (it can catch fire), ignite (degrees: a dry voxel this hot catches fire), flame (degrees: how hot it burns), fuel (seconds it burns in the open air; inside, with no open face, it smoulders much longer), water (degrees of heat it takes to dry a voxel before it can catch fire; a wet object has more), conduct (how fast heat goes through it from voxel to voxel: part of the difference a second; leaves hardly pass it, there is air between them), after (what is left once its fuel is gone: char = it stays black, and it holds the voxels joined to it; gone = it turns black, then grey ash, and is gone where it is), charTime (after: gone: seconds it stays black and ash). A voxel of a material that is gone at the end, no longer joined to one that stays or to the ground, burns where it hangs or, if it does not catch fire, lets go alone and flutters down (systems/burn.js hang).
